props.title: Bend What Is Behind

B21.capture_spec: C09: scene_c09_shift.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. Window 0.52 x 0.42 at (0.20, 0.12); shift 0 until u = 0.56, then 0.10 by u = 0.90. Verified: 3,640 of 3,640 sampled pixels show the meadow at x + shift (for 0.1 and for -0.05).
B21.visual_intent: Act title 'Bend What Is Behind' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left (the 9-line shift shader); at right a real Godot window: one large window in a cream frame over the meadow. The shift uniform sweeps from 0 to 0.1 and the picture inside the frame slides sideways against the picture outside; the sand path breaks at the frame's edges. Label 'shift 0.1'.
B21.motion_claim: The picture inside the frame slides to the left while the picture outside stays put.

show.event: shift uniform highlighted; the sweep begins

B21.why: A real window sliding against its surroundings shows the break at the frame's edge, which an arrow only implies.

cues.label: sin: a smooth wave between -1 and 1

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · amount grown by script

B22.capture_spec: C10: scene_c10_ripple_still.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. Window 0.56 x 0.52 at (0.20, 0.08); amount 0 until u = 0.44, then 0.012 by u = 0.92. Verified: the tile edge in ten rows sits at 560 minus 0.01 sin(60 y) times 1280, within 0.5 px (0.6 in Compatibility; the edge is found to a whole pixel).
B22.visual_intent: Code card at left (the 10-line ripple shader without time); at right a real Godot window: a large window in a cream frame; as the amount grows the straight tile edges inside become a chevron of ripples and the flowers stretch sideways.
B22.motion_claim: Straight lines inside the frame start to ripple as the amount grows.
B22.runner_up: manim plot of sin(y) with rows shifted
B22.why: The real ripple is the claim; the plot would explain the function but not what a viewer will see in a game.

cues.label: TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game

B23.capture_spec: C11: scene_c11_ripple_time.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps (fixed tick, so TIME is repeatable), Forward+, length = the beat's audio. Same window as C10, amount 0.01.
B23.visual_intent: Code card at left (the 10-line ripple shader with TIME); at right the same large window with the ripples now travelling, live. Label 'time: one clock'.
B23.motion_claim: The ripples travel through the window, in step across it.

show.event: the sine line with TIME highlighted

B23.why: Travel is motion; stills cannot show it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · amount swept by script

B24.capture_spec: C12: scene_c12_amount.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. As C11; amount 0.002 rising to 0.01 by u = 0.30, held to u = 0.60, then to 0.06 by u = 0.95.
B24.visual_intent: Code card at left with the amount line lit; at right the travelling-ripple window while amount sweeps: calm ripples at 0.01, then the picture shears into streaks at 0.06. Readouts '0.01' then '0.06'.
B24.motion_claim: The ripples grow from calm to torn as the number grows.
B24.why: Seeing the picture tear is the lesson; a number alone does not say how much is too much.

cues.label: mipmap: smaller, blurrier copies of a texture

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · blur level swept by script

B25.capture_spec: C13: scene_c13_blur.gd, NATIVE route: a 1920 x 1080 SubViewport at scale 1, the scene built for a 1920 x 1080 canvas (--native; NOT the 4K route, see CAPTURE-PLAN.md 'Routes'), 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. Window 0.56 x 0.56 at (0.20, 0.14); blur 0 until u = 0.58, then exactly 4.0 by u = 0.84, held. Verified: largest step between neighbouring pixels 0.377 at level 0, 0.012 at level 2, 0.008 at level 4 (1280 x 720 window, verify4 L8a); mean difference between the level-4 picture and the sharp one inside the window 0.028 on this route, 0.017 on the 4K route, 0.037 in a plain 1280 x 720 window (verify10 A).
B25.visual_intent: Code card at left (the 9-line blur shader; the declaration runs over two lines); at right a real Godot window: a large window in a cream frame; as the blur level rises from 0 to 4 the meadow inside turns to frosted glass while the picture outside stays sharp. Label 'level 4' once the level has reached it.
B25.motion_claim: The picture inside the frame blurs progressively as the level rises.

show.event: textureLod line highlighted; the sweep begins

B25.why: Frosted glass appearing is the whole claim; the stack of smaller copies is explained by the narration.

B26.capture_spec: C14: scene_c14_ride_glued.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps, Forward+, length = the beat's audio. WorldRoot (meadow with a 2-cell bleed + both windows) moves down 140 px between u = 0.12 and 0.52 and back by u = 0.96. Windows 0.30 x 0.46 at (0.08, 0.14) with 13-ripple-ride and at (0.58, 0.14) with 09-ripple-still; no TIME. Verified: after a 100 px move the glued window's edge offsets are unchanged in 6 of 6 rows; the ride window's changed in 6 of 6.
B26.visual_intent: Two windows in cream frames over a meadow that scrolls down and back. Left: ripples from the window's own address (UV.y); right: ripples from the screen address (SCREEN_UV.y). Both ripple fields are frozen. Labels 'UV: rides along' and 'screen UV: stays'; small labels 'UV.y' and 'SCREEN_UV.y' under the windows.
B26.motion_claim: On the left the ripples move down with the window; on the right they stay at the same screen rows while the window slides over them.

show.event: label 'UV: rides along' on the left window
label 'screen UV: stays' on the right window

B26.why: Relative motion between a window and its ripples is the claim and needs the real thing moving; plots would not show it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · live; colour changed by script at the end

B27.capture_spec: C15: scene_c15_pool_tint.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps (fixed tick), Forward+, length = the beat's audio. Pool 0.40 x 0.40 at (0.06, 0.52) with 11-water; water = (0.2, 0.5, 0.8) until u = 0.78, then to (0.6, 0.3, 0.8) by u = 0.94. Verified: pool pixel = 0.5 x meadow + 0.5 x water (both renderers); the shader reports a colour hint (no alpha) for water.
B27.visual_intent: Code card at left (the 12-line water shader); at right a real Godot window: the pool, a plain rectangle in the lower left, tinted blue over the bent meadow, rippling live. Near the end the water colour changes blue to violet, as an artist would with the colour picker.
B27.motion_claim: The pool ripples and, at the end, its colour changes from blue to violet.
B27.why: The tinted, rippling pool is the result and the colour change is the reason for the hint; both are only real in a render.

B28.capture_spec: C01 again (see B01): reuse the same video file. Verified: the first changed row down the pool is a different UV.y at five columns (0.080 to 0.115 in Forward+) and the meadow above it is untouched.
B28.visual_intent: Code card at left (the 14-line pool shader); at right the same pool capture as the opening: the wavy top edge ripples, and above it the grass shows through.
B28.motion_claim: The top edge of the pool undulates while the grass above it stays untouched.
B28.why: A wavy edge is only an edge when it moves.

B29.capture_spec: C16: scene_c16_pan.gd, 1280 x 720 canvas through the 4K SubViewport route, 30 fps (fixed tick), Forward+, length = the beat's audio. WorldRoot (meadow with a 2-cell bleed, the 12-pool pool, the player) moves down 110 px between u = 0.54 and 0.74 and back between u = 0.80 and 0.98.
B29.visual_intent: A real Godot window: the meadow, the finished pool and the player all scroll down together and back. The pool's ripples travel with the pool. Label 'pool scrolls too'.
B29.motion_claim: The whole scene pans and the pool stays glued to the ground, rippling.
B29.why: A pan is motion and the pool riding the ground is the claim.
